title: Previous Windows installation (Windows.old)
whyItMatters: An in-place upgrade can leave the previous Windows installation and its user files at the drive root, including the old profile data.
source: Microsoft Learn: Windows.old folder is created at the system drive root during an in-place Windows upgrade
notes: Large tree with a 20000-entry cap; truncation is reported if exceeded. The path jail still applies inside the old tree, and no file is opened.

cleanup.exportFirst: Copy anything still needed from the old profile folders inside this tree first; those files are deleted with it.
steps: Look through the old profile folders named in the plan and copy out anything you still need.
Open Settings > System > Storage > Cleanup recommendations.
Select Previous Windows installation(s) and remove them, then check the folder named in the plan is gone.
cleanup.risk: Deletes the previous Windows installation, including the old profile folders inside it. The previous Windows version can no longer be restored.
cleanup.source: Microsoft Support, Free up drive space in Windows: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/storage-filemanagement/free-up-drive-space-in-windows
